items.stem: A 29-year-old woman who is not immune to rubella on a preconception screen plans to conceive within the next few months. She has no allergies and is not pregnant today. Which is the best next step?
options: Give the vaccine now and continue trying to conceive without delay
Defer vaccination until immediately after delivery of the first pregnancy
Give rubella immune globulin monthly until she becomes pregnant
Give measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine now; delay conception 4 weeks
items.explanation: Rubella infection in early pregnancy can cause congenital rubella syndrome, so nonimmune women should be vaccinated before conception. The vaccine is a live attenuated one, so pregnancy should be avoided for 4 weeks afterward. Waiting until the postpartum period leaves the first pregnancy unprotected, and inadvertent vaccination should not alarm a patient but is not a plan. Immune globulin does not provide durable protection and is not used for prevention here.

items.stem: A 17-year-old has never had a period. She is 168 cm tall with normal breast development, scant pubic and axillary hair, and a blind vaginal pouch. Pelvic ultrasonography shows no uterus. Which finding is most likely?
options: A 46,XY karyotype with testosterone in the typical male range
A 45,X karyotype with elevated follicle-stimulating hormone
A 46,XX karyotype with estradiol in the typical female range
A 46,XY karyotype with low testosterone and absent breast tissue
items.explanation: Complete androgen insensitivity presents as primary amenorrhea with normal breasts, sparse body hair, a short blind vagina, and no uterus because anti-mullerian hormone from the testes regressed the mullerian ducts. Testes make male-range testosterone that is aromatized to estrogen. Turner syndrome has short stature and streak gonads, mullerian agenesis has normal hair and a 46,XX karyotype, and low testosterone with absent breasts does not fit this phenotype.

items.stem: A 26-year-old primigravida in the second stage of labor asks for perineal anesthesia before an anticipated outlet forceps delivery. Which landmark guides placement of a transvaginal pudendal nerve block?
options: The ischial tuberosity, with injection at the level of the vaginal introitus
The ischial spine, injecting just behind it near the sacrospinous ligament
The pubic symphysis, with injection along the superior pubic ramus
The sacral promontory, with injection along the iliopectineal line
items.explanation: The pudendal nerve (S2 to S4) loops around the ischial spine and sacrospinous ligament before entering the pudendal canal. Injecting there anesthetizes the lower vagina, vulva, and perineum. The tuberosity lies too far inferior and lateral to reach the nerve trunk, the symphysis and pubic ramus relate to the obturator and ilioinguinal regions, and the sacral promontory is an obstetric landmark for the pelvic inlet, not a site for blocking the perineal nerve.

items.stem: A 62-year-old woman smoked one pack daily for 30 years and quit 8 years ago. She has no cough or weight loss. Which screening test is recommended for her?
options: Chest radiography every year
Sputum cytology every 2 years
Annual low-dose chest computed tomography
No screening, because she stopped smoking
items.explanation: Lung cancer screening with annual low-dose computed tomography applies to adults aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years. She has 30 pack-years and quit 8 years ago, so she qualifies. Plain chest radiography and sputum cytology do not reduce mortality, and quitting does not remove eligibility until 15 years have passed.

items.stem: A surgeon plans to place a lateral 5 mm trocar for a laparoscopic hysterectomy. Which structure is the most important to avoid by transilluminating the abdominal wall and placing the port lateral to the rectus border?
options: The superficial circumflex iliac artery
The inferior epigastric artery and vein
The deep circumflex iliac vein
The external pudendal artery
items.explanation: The inferior epigastric vessels arise from the external iliac vessels, run behind the rectus muscle, and lie lateral to the rectus border in the lower abdomen, so lateral ports risk laceration and rectus sheath hematoma. Direct visualization of the vessels from inside, and placement lateral to them, prevents injury. The circumflex iliac vessels sit near the inguinal ligament and the external pudendal artery supplies the groin and vulva, so these are not usual port-site hazards.

items.stem: A 34-year-old G3P2 at 28 weeks has an Rh-negative blood type with a negative antibody screen. Her husband is Rh-positive. Which plan is correct?
options: Give anti-D immune globulin at 28 weeks and again after delivery if the newborn is Rh-positive
Give anti-D immune globulin only if an antibody screen becomes positive
Give anti-D immune globulin once at term only
Withhold anti-D immune globulin because her previous children were unaffected
items.explanation: An unsensitized Rh-negative woman receives 300 mcg of anti-D immune globulin at about 28 weeks, and a second dose within 72 hours of birth if the neonate is Rh-positive. Once she has formed anti-D antibodies, prophylaxis is of no use, so it must be given before sensitization occurs. Prior unaffected pregnancies do not protect against sensitization in this one.

items.stem: A 52-year-old woman completed treatment for estrogen receptor positive breast cancer 2 years ago and takes tamoxifen. She has frequent disruptive hot flushes. Which therapy is most appropriate?
options: Systemic estradiol with a progestogen
Paroxetine
Conjugated estrogens with bazedoxifene
Venlafaxine
items.explanation: Systemic estrogen is contraindicated after hormone-sensitive breast cancer. Venlafaxine, a serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, reduces vasomotor symptoms and has little effect on tamoxifen metabolism. Paroxetine is a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor that blocks conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite and should be avoided, and the estrogen with bazedoxifene combination still contains estrogen and is not recommended in this setting.

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman at 6 weeks of gestation underwent computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis for appendicitis; the estimated fetal dose was 25 mGy. She asks whether the baby will have birth defects. What is the best counseling?
options: The dose in early pregnancy makes major malformations very likely
Termination should be discussed because any imaging dose is teratogenic
The dose is below the 50 mGy level at which anomalies are expected to rise
The risk is negligible only if the scan had been done after 20 weeks
items.explanation: Fetal doses under 50 mGy are not associated with an increase in malformations, growth restriction, or pregnancy loss, and a single abdominopelvic scan usually delivers 10 to 25 mGy. Deterministic harm appears only above that threshold, and the all-or-none period of the first two weeks after conception does not apply here. Recommending termination for such a dose is not supported, and later timing does not change the conclusion.

items.stem: A 30-year-old man who is transgender has taken testosterone for 4 years and has had no hysterectomy. He has never had cervical screening. Which recommendation is correct?
options: Cervical screening is unnecessary after testosterone therapy
Begin cervical cytology at the same age and interval as for other patients with a cervix
Screen annually with cytology for as long as he takes testosterone
Delay screening until he has stopped taking testosterone
items.explanation: Screening follows the anatomy: anyone with a cervix needs cervical cancer screening on the same schedule, with cytology every 3 years from age 21 to 29 and from age 30 cytology, primary HPV testing, or cotesting at the usual intervals. Testosterone causes epithelial atrophy that can make cytology inadequate, so clinicians may note the therapy on the requisition, but it does not remove the need for screening or require stopping treatment.

items.stem: A 148-kg woman undergoes an abdominal hysterectomy for fibroids. Which prophylactic antibiotic regimen is most appropriate?
options: Cefazolin 1 g intravenously given about 30 minutes after the skin incision is made
Vancomycin alone intravenously 12 hours before surgery
Cefazolin 3 g intravenously within 60 minutes before incision
Oral amoxicillin given the night before the operation
items.explanation: First-generation cephalosporins are first-line prophylaxis for hysterectomy, given within 60 minutes before incision to have tissue levels when the skin is opened. Patients who weigh 120 kg or more receive 3 g rather than 2 g. Post-incision dosing and dosing the night before lose the benefit, and vancomycin alone does not cover the gram-negative and anaerobic organisms of the vaginal flora.

items.stem: A 31-year-old G1P0 at 34 weeks has an estimated fetal weight at the 8th percentile. Amniotic fluid and umbilical artery Doppler studies are normal. Which management is best?
options: Immediate delivery now at 34 weeks
Reassurance with routine care and no additional surveillance
Delivery at 32 weeks to prevent progression to absent end-diastolic flow
Serial growth scans with weekly testing and delivery at 38 to 39 weeks
items.explanation: An estimated weight between the 3rd and 10th percentile with normal Doppler and fluid is small for gestational age and carries a modest risk. It is followed by interval growth ultrasonography, weekly or twice weekly fetal testing, and delivery between 38 and 39 weeks. Immediate delivery is reserved for abnormal Doppler or deterioration, and observation with no testing misses a group at higher risk of stillbirth.

items.stem: A 21-year-old woman with a normal body mass index requests emergency contraception 80 hours after unprotected intercourse. She declines an intrauterine device. Which oral option is most effective?
options: Ulipristal acetate 30 mg as a single dose
Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg as a single dose
A combined oral contraceptive regimen taken in two doses
No oral method works beyond 72 hours
items.explanation: Ulipristal acetate remains effective up to 120 hours after intercourse and is more effective than levonorgestrel, particularly later in the window. Levonorgestrel is labeled for 72 hours and loses efficacy as time passes. Combined pill regimens are less effective and cause more nausea. The belief that nothing works after 72 hours is incorrect and would wrongly deny her an effective option.

items.stem: A study reports that women whose cancer was found by a new screening test lived 7 years after diagnosis, compared with 4 years in unscreened women, yet cancer deaths per 1,000 women were identical in both groups. Which bias best explains this?
options: Length-time bias
Recall bias
Selection bias in the control group
Lead-time bias
items.explanation: Screening moves the date of diagnosis earlier without delaying death, so survival measured from diagnosis looks longer even when nothing has changed in the course of disease. Identical mortality in both groups shows there was no true benefit. Length-time bias concerns overrepresentation of slow, indolent tumors among screen-detected cases, recall bias applies to retrospective exposure reporting, and selection bias would need unequal group composition.

items.stem: A 21-year-old woman has a positive nucleic acid test for chlamydia on routine screening. She is not pregnant and has no drug allergies. Which treatment is recommended?
options: Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 7 days
Azithromycin 500 mg orally once daily for 3 days
Ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscularly as a single dose
Metronidazole 2 g orally as a single dose
items.explanation: Doxycycline for 7 days is the preferred regimen for uncomplicated chlamydia in nonpregnant patients, with better cure rates for rectal infection than azithromycin. A single 1 g dose of azithromycin is the alternative, and it is the choice in pregnancy because doxycycline is avoided. Ceftriaxone treats gonorrhea, not chlamydia, and metronidazole treats trichomoniasis and bacterial vaginosis. Partners should be treated and she should be retested in 3 months.

items.stem: During a pelvic lymph node dissection for cervical cancer, the nerve in the obturator fossa is transected. Which finding is expected on the first postoperative day?
options: Foot drop with numbness over the dorsum of the foot
Loss of knee extension with an absent patellar reflex
Weak thigh adduction with numbness of the medial thigh
Numbness over the lateral thigh without weakness
items.explanation: The obturator nerve supplies the adductor muscles and a patch of skin on the medial thigh, so transection weakens adduction and leaves medial thigh numbness. Foot drop reflects common peroneal injury from lithotomy compression. Loss of knee extension with a lost patellar reflex indicates femoral nerve injury, and isolated lateral thigh numbness is lateral femoral cutaneous nerve entrapment.

items.stem: A 36-year-old G2P1 at 37 0/7 weeks has blood pressure of 148/94 mm Hg on two occasions 5 hours apart and 0.6 g of protein in a 24-hour urine collection. She has no headache, and platelets, creatinine, and liver enzymes are normal. What is the best management?
options: Continued expectant management until 40 weeks with twice weekly visits
Delivery now
Intravenous magnesium sulfate and cesarean delivery within the hour
Oral labetalol and discharge with a plan to deliver at 41 weeks
items.explanation: This is preeclampsia without severe features, since pressures are under 160/110 and laboratory results are normal. Delivery is recommended at 37 0/7 weeks, because the maternal risk of progression outweighs any benefit of prolonging pregnancy beyond that point. Cesarean birth is not required and magnesium is reserved for severe features, so neither is needed urgently. Waiting until 40 or 41 weeks exposes her to seizure, abruption, and HELLP.

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome has had oligomenorrhea since menarche. She wishes to conceive. Her BMI is 31 kg/m2 and tubal patency and her partner's semen analysis are normal. Which is the best first-line medication for ovulation induction?
options: Clomiphene citrate at a standard dose
Metformin as the single agent
Letrozole
Human menopausal gonadotropin injections
items.explanation: Letrozole is now the first-line agent for ovulation induction in polycystic ovary syndrome, with higher live birth rates and fewer multiple gestations than clomiphene. Clomiphene remains an alternative, metformin alone is a weak ovulation inducer and mostly addresses metabolic features, and gonadotropins are second-line agents with a higher risk of multiple gestation and hyperstimulation. Lifestyle change and weight loss are encouraged in parallel.

items.stem: A competent 33-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks declines recommended cesarean birth for a breech presentation after a full discussion of the risks. She wants to attempt vaginal breech delivery. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Obtain a court order to authorize the operation at once
Perform the cesarean while she is sedated for labor analgesia
Ask her husband or another close relative to sign consent for the cesarean on her behalf
Respect her informed refusal and offer the best support for the plan she chooses
items.explanation: A pregnant patient with decision-making capacity has the same right to refuse treatment as any other adult, even when the clinician believes the refusal risks the fetus. The physician continues to counsel, documents the discussion, and provides the safest care for her chosen course. Judicial or surrogate authorization, or operating without valid consent, overrides autonomy and is not ethically acceptable in this circumstance.

items.stem: A 70-year-old woman has taken oral alendronate for 5 years. She has had no fractures, and her femoral neck T-score is now -2.0. What is the appropriate plan?
options: Continue the bisphosphonate for another 20 years
Consider a drug holiday after 5 years of therapy
Switch to daily teriparatide
Stop calcium and vitamin D supplements
items.explanation: After 5 years of oral bisphosphonate, a woman without fractures and with a hip T-score above -2.5 is at low fracture risk, so a drug holiday is reasonable because fracture protection persists after stopping. Continuing for decades raises the risk of atypical femur fracture and osteonecrosis. Teriparatide is for very high risk, and calcium and vitamin D should continue.

items.stem: During hysteroscopic resection of a submucosal fibroid using glycine as the distending medium, the fluid deficit reaches 1,500 mL. The anesthesiologist reports a falling oxygen saturation and the patient becomes confused. What is the best next step?
options: Stop the procedure and measure serum sodium
Increase the infusion pressure to improve visualization
Continue until the fibroid is finished and then check labs
Give a rapid bolus of hypotonic fluid
items.explanation: Electrolyte-free media such as glycine are absorbed through venous sinuses and cause hypervolemia and dilutional hyponatremia, with confusion, pulmonary edema, and seizures. A deficit of 1,000 mL of these fluids is the common stopping threshold, versus 2,500 mL for saline. The procedure is stopped, sodium is measured, and diuretics are given cautiously. Higher pressure increases absorption, and hypotonic fluid worsens the hyponatremia.

items.stem: A 33-year-old G2P2 delivered 8 weeks ago after a pregnancy complicated by gestational diabetes treated with diet alone. She is breastfeeding. Which test best assesses her current glucose status?
options: A random plasma glucose measured at the next annual visit
Hemoglobin A1c alone
A 75 g oral glucose tolerance test with a 2-hour value
A 50 g glucose challenge test with a 1-hour value
items.explanation: Women with gestational diabetes should have a 75 g, 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test between 4 and 12 weeks postpartum to detect persistent diabetes or prediabetes, and lifelong screening at least every 3 years follows. Hemoglobin A1c is less reliable after the blood loss and red cell turnover of the puerperium. The 50 g challenge is a screening test for pregnancy, and a random glucose lacks sensitivity.

items.stem: A 37-year-old woman and her husband have not conceived after 8 months of regular unprotected intercourse. Her cycles are regular. She has no known pelvic disease. What is the best next step?
options: Reassure the couple and wait until 12 months have elapsed
Proceed directly to in vitro fertilization without any testing
Perform diagnostic laparoscopy before any other testing
Begin a fertility evaluation now rather than waiting longer
items.explanation: Evaluation starts after 12 months of trying for women under 35, after 6 months for women 35 to 39, and immediately for women 40 or older or those with known risk factors. At 37 she qualifies for earlier testing, which includes ovarian reserve, tubal assessment, ovulation confirmation, and semen analysis. Skipping testing for in vitro fertilization or doing laparoscopy first is not appropriate, and further waiting costs time.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman whose brother has Duchenne muscular dystrophy is found by molecular testing to carry the same pathogenic dystrophin variant. Her partner is unaffected. What is the risk to each of her future children?
options: All sons affected and all daughters carriers, because the variant is on the maternal X
Half of sons affected and half of daughters carriers
Half of daughters affected and no affected sons, since males are protected
No child affected, because the partner does not carry the variant
items.explanation: For an X-linked recessive disorder, a carrier mother transmits the variant X to half of her gametes. A son who receives it has no second X to compensate and is affected, so half of sons are expected to be affected. A daughter who receives it is usually a carrier because the partner provides a normal X. Affected daughters would require an affected father, and certain disease in every son would imply a homozygous mother.

items.stem: A 19-year-old college student was sexually assaulted 36 hours ago by an unknown person and presents to the emergency department. She is not on contraception and has no allergies. Which care is most appropriate in addition to offering an evidence collection kit?
options: Emergency contraception alone, with testing for sexually transmitted infections at the 2 week visit
Reassurance and follow-up in 6 months for screening
HIV prophylaxis only, because other infections are rare
Emergency contraception and prophylaxis against chlamydia, gonorrhea, trichomoniasis, and HIV
items.explanation: Care is trauma-informed and the survivor chooses whether to have evidence collected. Presumptive treatment covers chlamydia, gonorrhea, and trichomoniasis, emergency contraception is offered up to 120 hours, and HIV postexposure prophylaxis is offered within 72 hours of substantial exposure and continues for 28 days. Delaying treatment risks loss to follow-up and missed prophylaxis windows, and one agent does not cover all of the risks.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman 3 weeks after a total laparoscopic hysterectomy resumed intercourse and has sudden pelvic pain with a watery vaginal discharge. Examination shows loops of bowel protruding from the vagina. What is the immediate management?
options: Cover the bowel with moist sterile dressings, give antibiotics, and go to the operating room
Reduce the bowel manually in the clinic, give oral antibiotics, and send her home the same day
Pack the vagina with dry gauze and begin oral antibiotics
Observe in the hospital with bowel rest alone for 48 hours
items.explanation: Vaginal cuff dehiscence with evisceration is a surgical emergency, because exposed bowel may be ischemic or injured. The bowel is protected with warm moist sterile dressings, the patient is kept fasting, broad-spectrum antibiotics are started, and the cuff is repaired in the operating room, with bowel resection if needed. Sexual intercourse early after hysterectomy is a recognized risk. Office reduction, dry packing, or observation risks infarction and peritonitis.

items.stem: A 22-year-old G1P0 at 24 weeks has flank pain, fever of 39.1 C, and costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteria. Her vital signs are stable and she vomits when taking oral fluids. What is the best treatment?
options: Outpatient nitrofurantoin for 7 days with a repeat culture
A single oral dose of fosfomycin and a return visit in a week
Hospital admission with intravenous ceftriaxone
Intravenous gentamicin alone with a plan to discharge the next morning
items.explanation: Pyelonephritis in pregnancy requires admission, intravenous fluids, and a parenteral antibiotic such as a cephalosporin until she is afebrile, then oral therapy to complete 10 to 14 days, followed by suppression for the rest of the pregnancy. Nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin reach poor tissue levels in the kidney and are only suitable for cystitis. Aminoglycoside monotherapy is not the standard approach.

items.stem: A 49-year-old G3P3 woman with a BMI of 38 kg/m2 has had irregular heavy vaginal bleeding for 5 months. Pregnancy test is negative and hemoglobin is 11.0 g/dL. Which is the best next step?
options: Endometrial biopsy
Tranexamic acid with no further evaluation
Repeat evaluation after two normal cycles
Hysterectomy without any tissue sampling
items.explanation: Sampling is indicated for abnormal uterine bleeding at age 45 or older, and in younger women with obesity, unopposed estrogen exposure, or persistent bleeding, because of the risk of hyperplasia and cancer. Anovulation with obesity increases that risk. Medical therapy can follow only after malignancy is excluded, waiting wastes time, and hysterectomy without a tissue diagnosis can result in incorrect surgical planning.

items.stem: A healthy 31-year-old woman at 34 weeks of gestation has an arterial blood gas drawn for an unrelated reason. Which result is typical of normal late pregnancy?
options: pH 7.40, PaCO2 40 mm Hg, bicarbonate 24 mEq/L
pH 7.43, PaCO2 30 mm Hg, bicarbonate 20 mEq/L
pH 7.35, PaCO2 48 mm Hg, bicarbonate 26 mEq/L
pH 7.50, PaCO2 40 mm Hg, bicarbonate 30 mEq/L
items.explanation: Progesterone raises minute ventilation, producing a compensated respiratory alkalosis with PaCO2 near 27 to 32 mm Hg, slightly alkaline pH, and renal bicarbonate loss to roughly 18 to 21 mEq/L. A nonpregnant profile with PaCO2 of 40 is not expected. Hypercapnia with a low pH suggests respiratory failure. A metabolic alkalosis with high bicarbonate points to vomiting or diuretics.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman has severe irritability, depressed mood, and anxiety that begin about 5 days before each period and resolve within 2 days after bleeding starts. Prospective daily ratings for two cycles confirm the pattern. What is the best initial treatment?
options: A benzodiazepine taken daily
Danazol throughout the cycle
Bilateral oophorectomy
A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
items.explanation: Symptoms confined to the luteal phase that impair function and are confirmed prospectively define premenstrual dysphoric disorder. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, given continuously or only in the luteal phase, are first-line, and drospirenone-containing combined pills are another option. Daily benzodiazepines carry dependence risk and are not recommended, and danazol and oophorectomy are reserved for refractory cases because of their adverse effects.

items.stem: A 63-year-old woman with a body mass index of 36 kg/m2 is scheduled for open hysterectomy and staging for endometrial cancer, expected to last 4 hours. She has no history of thrombosis and a normal creatinine. Which venous thromboembolism prophylaxis is most appropriate?
options: Mechanical plus pharmacologic prophylaxis, extended for up to 4 weeks
Early ambulation alone
Sequential compression devices alone until she walks
Aspirin 81 mg daily for 2 weeks
items.explanation: Age over 60, malignancy, obesity, and a long operation place her in the high risk category, where mechanical and pharmacologic prophylaxis are combined, and after major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery prophylaxis is extended for up to four weeks to lower late clots. Ambulation alone suits low risk patients, compression devices alone suit moderate risk, and aspirin is not an adequate substitute for anticoagulant prophylaxis.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman with hypothyroidism takes levothyroxine 100 mcg daily. Her home pregnancy test is positive at about 5 weeks. Her TSH was normal 3 months ago. What should she do now?
options: Continue the same dose and recheck TSH at the 20-week visit
Increase the daily dose by about 25 to 30 percent and recheck TSH in 4 weeks
Stop levothyroxine until the end of the first trimester
Switch to propylthiouracil for the first trimester
items.explanation: Estrogen raises thyroxine-binding globulin and fetal demands rise, so levothyroxine requirements climb by 25 to 30 percent early in pregnancy. Patients are advised to increase the dose as soon as the test is positive, then TSH is checked every 4 weeks in the first half of pregnancy. Stopping therapy risks fetal neurocognitive harm and miscarriage, and propylthiouracil is an antithyroid drug for hyperthyroidism that would worsen hypothyroidism.

items.stem: A 34-year-old nulligravida with heavy menstrual bleeding and infertility has a 3 cm submucosal leiomyoma that distorts the endometrial cavity. She desires pregnancy. Which treatment is most appropriate?
options: Uterine artery embolization
Abdominal hysterectomy
Hysteroscopic resection of the fibroid
Long-term GnRH agonist therapy before conception
items.explanation: Submucosal fibroids that distort the cavity cause bleeding and impair implantation, and hysteroscopic myomectomy is minimally invasive and preserves fertility. Embolization is not recommended for women who want pregnancy because of concerns about ovarian reserve and placentation. Hysterectomy ends fertility, and GnRH agonists shrink fibroids temporarily and induce hypoestrogenism, so symptoms and size return after therapy stops.

items.stem: In a randomized trial of surgery versus medical therapy, several women assigned to surgery crossed over to medical therapy. Which analysis best preserves the benefits of randomization?
options: Intention-to-treat analysis
Per-protocol analysis
As-treated analysis
Exclusion of all crossovers
items.explanation: Intention-to-treat analysis keeps every participant in the group to which she was randomized, regardless of what she ultimately received, which preserves the balance of known and unknown confounders created by randomization. Per-protocol, as-treated, and exclusion approaches break that balance and usually exaggerate treatment effects because those who cross over differ systematically from those who do not.

items.stem: A 46-year-old woman with no family history of cancer and no symptoms asks about colorectal cancer screening. She has never been screened. Which is an acceptable screening option?
options: Colonoscopy only after age 60
Colonoscopy every 10 years
Annual serum carcinoembryonic antigen testing
Digital rectal examination in the clinic each year
items.explanation: Average-risk adults are screened from age 45 to 75 with colonoscopy every 10 years, annual fecal immunochemical or high-sensitivity stool tests, or other recommended options. Delaying until 60 misses the recommended window. Carcinoembryonic antigen is a tumor marker used to follow known disease, not a screening test, and a single rectal examination in the office has poor sensitivity for colorectal cancer.

items.stem: On postoperative day 2 after abdominal hysterectomy for cancer, a woman has sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, heart rate 118, and oxygen saturation 90 percent on room air. The chest radiograph is clear. What is the best next step?
options: Serum D-dimer to exclude embolism
Observation with incentive spirometry
Computed tomography pulmonary angiography, with anticoagulation if suspicion is high
Prophylactic antibiotics for pneumonia
items.explanation: Sudden dyspnea with tachycardia and hypoxemia after major pelvic cancer surgery is pulmonary embolism until proven otherwise, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography is the diagnostic test, with empiric anticoagulation if suspicion is high and imaging is delayed. D-dimer is nonspecific after surgery and useless for exclusion here. Observation or antibiotics would delay life-saving treatment. Delays in treatment increase mortality from large emboli.

items.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 35 weeks has generalized itching with no rash. Her peak total serum bile acids are 105 micromoles per liter, and the fetus is reactive. When is delivery recommended?
options: At 38 0/7 weeks
At 39 0/7 weeks
At 40 0/7 weeks
At 36 0/7 weeks
items.explanation: In intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, stillbirth risk rises sharply when bile acids reach 100 micromoles per liter or more, so delivery is recommended at 36 0/7 weeks. When levels are below that, delivery between 36 and 39 weeks is individualized. Waiting until 38, 39, or 40 weeks exposes the fetus to the highest-risk period and is not appropriate with a level this high.

items.stem: A 58-year-old woman has a 5 cm solid ovarian mass. Pathology shows nests of transitional-type epithelial cells with grooved, coffee-bean nuclei within dense fibrous stroma. Which tumor is most likely?
options: Fibroma
Mucinous cystadenoma
Brenner tumor
Dysgerminoma
items.explanation: A Brenner tumor is an epithelial ovarian neoplasm made of transitional-type cells resembling urothelium, with grooved nuclei in a fibrous stroma, and it is usually benign and found in older women. A fibroma lacks epithelial nests, a mucinous cystadenoma is lined by mucin-secreting columnar cells, and a dysgerminoma shows sheets of large clear cells with lymphocytes in young women.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman at 27 weeks is found to have a placenta accreta spectrum disorder on imaging. She is currently at a level I facility with no blood bank beyond emergency release. What is the most appropriate system-level action?
options: Transfer now for delivery at a level III or IV center
Continue care locally and transfer only if bleeding begins
Schedule delivery at the nearest level II hospital at 34 weeks
Arrange a planned vaginal delivery to avoid an abdominal incision
items.explanation: Levels of maternal care direct women with accreta spectrum to a level III or IV facility with subspecialty surgeons, blood bank capacity, and intensive care, and planned antenatal transfer is preferred over emergency transfer. Waiting for bleeding risks hemorrhage during transport. A level II hospital lacks the required resources. Vaginal delivery with an invasive placenta risks catastrophic hemorrhage and is not a safer plan.

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman who has never received human papillomavirus vaccine asks about vaccination. She is not pregnant and is immunocompetent. Which schedule is recommended?
options: Two doses given 6 to 12 months apart
A single dose with no booster
No vaccine, because she has probably already been exposed
Three doses at 0, 1 to 2, and 6 months
items.explanation: Catch-up vaccination is recommended through age 26 for anyone not adequately vaccinated, and prior sexual activity does not remove the benefit. A series started at age 15 or older requires three doses at 0, 1 to 2, and 6 months. Two doses are sufficient only when the series begins before the 15th birthday in an immunocompetent person. A single dose or no vaccine leaves her unprotected against types she has not yet acquired.

items.stem: During an abdominal hysterectomy, the surgeon clamps the uterine vessels at the level of the cervix. Which structure lies directly beneath the uterine artery at this point and is at greatest risk of injury?
options: The internal iliac vein
The ureter
The obturator nerve
The inferior epigastric artery
items.explanation: The ureter passes under the uterine artery about 1.5 to 2 cm lateral to the cervix, often described as water under the bridge, so it is vulnerable when pedicles are clamped near the cervix. The internal iliac vein and obturator nerve lie more laterally along the pelvic sidewall. The inferior epigastric artery is in the anterior abdominal wall and relevant to trocar placement.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 30 weeks has had a vesicular rash for 2 days, with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Varicella is diagnosed clinically, and her oxygen saturation is 92 percent on room air. Which is the best management?
options: Hospital admission with intravenous acyclovir
Varicella zoster immune globulin to treat the rash
Oral supportive care at home until the lesions crust
The live varicella vaccine to speed recovery
items.explanation: Varicella pneumonia is a serious cause of maternal death, so a pregnant woman with respiratory symptoms is admitted and given intravenous acyclovir promptly. Immune globulin is only for postexposure prevention in susceptible women and does not treat established disease. Supportive home care risks deterioration, and the live vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy and offers no treatment benefit.

items.stem: A 61-year-old woman has had one episode of vaginal spotting 10 years after menopause. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows an endometrial thickness of 3 mm. She takes no hormones. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Endometrial biopsy in all cases
Dilation and curettage in the operating room
Reassurance and follow-up if bleeding recurs
Total hysterectomy with salpingo-oophorectomy
items.explanation: Evaluation of postmenopausal bleeding starts with transvaginal ultrasonography or endometrial biopsy. A thickness of 4 mm or less carries a very low risk of cancer, so observation is acceptable if bleeding does not recur, and biopsy is done if it persists or recurs. Biopsy for every patient is not required after a reassuring scan, and curettage or hysterectomy would be excessive without any tissue diagnosis.

items.stem: A healthy 19-year-old woman requests a combined oral contraceptive pill. She has no symptoms, no pelvic complaints, and has never had cervical screening. What evaluation is required before prescribing it?
options: A bimanual pelvic examination and speculum examination
A blood pressure measurement and medical history
A cervical cytology sample taken at the same visit
A baseline transvaginal ultrasonography of the ovaries
items.explanation: Safe prescribing of combined hormonal contraception depends on the medical history and a blood pressure measurement, which together screen for the contraindications that matter. A pelvic or speculum examination is not needed to prescribe contraception, and cervical screening does not begin until age 21 and is not a prerequisite. Routine ultrasonography has no role, and requiring unnecessary examinations creates a barrier to effective contraception.

items.stem: On postoperative day 7 after a midline laparotomy, a woman coughs and a gush of pink fluid drains from the incision, with loops of bowel visible in the wound. What is the immediate step?
options: Push the bowel back and apply an adhesive strip
Bed rest with dry gauze and observation
Bedside skin closure under local anesthetic
Cover the bowel with moist sterile saline dressings and arrange return to the operating room
items.explanation: Fascial dehiscence with evisceration is a surgical emergency. The exposed bowel is covered with warm, moist sterile saline dressings, the patient is kept nothing by mouth, antibiotics are started, and she is taken for operative closure. Reducing the bowel at the bedside under a strip, dry dressings, or skin closure alone leaves the fascial defect, risking bowel injury and infection.

items.stem: A 25-year-old G1P0 at 40 weeks has spontaneous rupture of membranes. She is dilated to 7 cm and 100 percent effaced with adequate contractions of 220 Montevideo units for 4 hours with no cervical change. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Continue observation for 4 more hours and recheck her dilation
Start oxytocin and reassess again in 6 hours
Cesarean delivery for arrest of labor in the active phase
Perform an operative vaginal delivery with outlet forceps
items.explanation: Active-phase arrest is diagnosed at 6 cm or more with ruptured membranes and no cervical change for 4 hours of adequate contractions, or 6 hours with oxytocin when contractions are inadequate. Adequacy here is already shown by more than 200 Montevideo units. Further waiting or oxytocin adds nothing, and forceps require a fully dilated cervix, so cesarean birth is the correct choice.

items.stem: A 20-year-old woman has fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness, and mucopurulent cervical discharge. She is hemodynamically stable and tolerates oral intake. Pregnancy test is negative. Which outpatient regimen is recommended?
options: Azithromycin as a single dose
Ceftriaxone, doxycycline, and metronidazole
Metronidazole alone for 7 days
Oral amoxicillin and clavulanate for 5 days
items.explanation: Mild to moderate pelvic inflammatory disease is treated with ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscularly once, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days, and metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 14 days to cover anaerobes. Treatment should not wait for confirmatory tests. A single agent misses gonorrhea, chlamydia, or anaerobes, and incomplete treatment increases the risk of tubal scarring and infertility. Partners are treated.

items.stem: A 25-year-old woman with a male partner who has HIV of uncertain viral suppression asks about preexposure prophylaxis. She has no symptoms and no known medical problems. Which step is required before starting?
options: A documented negative hepatitis A antibody test result
A full pelvic examination with a cervical culture
A baseline chest radiograph
A negative HIV test and renal function
items.explanation: Before tenofovir-based prophylaxis, HIV infection must be excluded with a laboratory test, because use in an infected person fosters resistance, and creatinine clearance should be checked since tenofovir can affect the kidneys. Hepatitis B status guides vaccination and the choice of agent, but hepatitis A serology is not needed. Pelvic examination and chest radiography are not prerequisites.

items.stem: A 51-year-old woman with abnormal uterine bleeding has an office endometrial biopsy showing scant proliferative endometrium without hyperplasia. Bleeding persists after 3 months of treatment, and ultrasonography suggests a 1.5 cm focal lesion in the fundus. What is the best next procedure?
options: Hysteroscopy with directed biopsy
Repeat blind office biopsy in 1 year
Endometrial ablation without further sampling
Blind dilation and curettage
items.explanation: An office suction biopsy detects diffuse disease reliably but can miss a focal lesion such as a polyp or small cancer, so a negative result with persistent bleeding calls for hysteroscopy with directed biopsy. Waiting a year delays the diagnosis, ablation should never precede exclusion of malignancy, and a blind curettage samples the cavity without seeing it and can miss the same focal lesion.

items.stem: A 32-year-old G2P1 at 40 weeks with one prior low transverse cesarean is admitted for a trial of labor induction. Her cervix is closed, long, and posterior with a Bishop score of 2. Which method of cervical ripening is most appropriate?
options: Misoprostol 25 mcg vaginally every 4 hours
Dinoprostone insert placed in the posterior fornix
Transcervical balloon catheter placement
High-dose oxytocin infusion started immediately
items.explanation: After a prior cesarean, prostaglandins raise the risk of uterine rupture and are avoided, so a mechanical method such as a balloon catheter is favored for ripening. Oxytocin may be used for labor after ripening, with careful titration, but starting it at high dose on an unripe cervix is unlikely to succeed and increases rupture risk. A Bishop score under 6 predicts failed induction without ripening.

items.stem: A 32-year-old premenopausal woman has an incidental 4 cm unilocular, anechoic ovarian cyst with a thin wall and no septations on ultrasonography done for another reason. She has no symptoms. What is the appropriate management?
options: No follow-up imaging is needed
Laparoscopic cystectomy within a month
CA-125 and repeat ultrasonography in 6 weeks
Oral contraceptives for 3 months to shrink the cyst
items.explanation: A simple cyst under 5 cm in a premenopausal woman is almost always benign and functional, and consensus guidance says no follow-up is needed. Surgery exposes her to risk without benefit. CA-125 is unreliable in premenopausal women and adds false positives. Oral contraceptives do not hasten resolution of existing functional cysts, so they offer no advantage here.

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 10 weeks smokes eight cigarettes daily and wants to quit. Which approach is first line?
options: Varenicline started now
Behavioral counseling with structured quit support
Switching to electronic cigarettes
Reducing to four cigarettes per day
items.explanation: In pregnancy, behavioral counseling is first-line treatment for tobacco cessation, with pharmacotherapy considered only if counseling fails and after weighing risks. Evidence on varenicline in pregnancy is limited. Electronic cigarettes are not recommended as a cessation aid, and cutting down does not substantially reduce fetal exposure to carbon monoxide and nicotine. Quit support should continue after delivery because relapse is common.

items.stem: A 29-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks in active labor has a fetal heart rate tracing with absent baseline variability and recurrent late decelerations for 40 minutes. There is no response to lateral positioning, fluid bolus, and stopping oxytocin. What is the best next step?
options: Continue observation for another hour with the same interventions
Begin amnioinfusion to relieve cord compression
Place a fetal scalp lactate order and wait for results before acting
Expedite delivery
items.explanation: Absent variability with recurrent late decelerations is a Category III tracing, which is associated with fetal acidemia. Resuscitative measures are applied while preparing for delivery, and if the tracing does not resolve promptly, delivery is expedited by the fastest safe route. Waiting adds risk of hypoxic injury. Amnioinfusion treats variable decelerations from cord compression, not late decelerations from uteroplacental insufficiency.

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman has severe dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain unresponsive to rest and has been diagnosed clinically with probable endometriosis. She is not seeking pregnancy now. What is the best initial treatment?
options: Laparoscopy with excision of all visible lesions before any trial of medical therapy
Nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs with a combined hormonal contraceptive
Hysterectomy with bilateral oophorectomy
Long-term opioid therapy as the principal treatment
items.explanation: Empiric therapy is appropriate when endometriosis is suspected clinically, without a surgical diagnosis. First-line therapy is a nonsteroidal drug plus continuous or cyclic combined hormonal contraception or a progestin. GnRH analogs and surgery are used when first-line therapy fails. Hysterectomy with oophorectomy is excessive for a young woman who may want children, and chronic opioids are not recommended for pelvic pain.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman at an annual visit scores positive on a brief partner violence screen and says her partner has threatened to harm her if she leaves. She does not want police involvement. What is the best response?
options: Offer a safety plan, resources, and follow-up support
Insist that she leave the relationship immediately
Report to the police against her wishes in all cases
Schedule couples counseling with her partner present at the visit
items.explanation: Care for intimate partner violence centers on safety, nonjudgmental support, documentation, and connection to advocates and shelters, while respecting the patient's autonomy, since leaving can be the most dangerous time. Mandatory police reporting in adults varies by jurisdiction and is not universal. Pressuring departure removes her control. Couples counseling is not safe, because it can provoke retaliation.

items.stem: After delivery of the fetal head in a 31-year-old G3P2 with diabetes, the head retracts against the perineum. The McRoberts position and suprapubic pressure are applied without success. What is the next step?
options: Apply strong fundal pressure to push the shoulder through
Cut the umbilical cord before the shoulders deliver
Perform immediate fundal massage and give oxytocin
Deliver the posterior arm
items.explanation: Shoulder dystocia is managed stepwise: call for help, McRoberts maneuver, and suprapubic pressure, followed by delivery of the posterior arm or rotational maneuvers, with the Zavanelli maneuver and symphysiotomy as last resorts. Fundal pressure worsens impaction and risks uterine rupture, and clamping the cord does not free the shoulder. Oxytocin and massage address atony after delivery and play no role in relieving the obstruction.

items.stem: A 48-year-old G3P3 reports leakage of urine with coughing and sneezing for 2 years, and no urgency. Pelvic examination shows good support, and urinalysis is normal. Her cough stress test is positive. She has tried pelvic floor training without enough benefit. What is the most appropriate procedure?
options: Anterior colporrhaphy with plication of the bladder neck
Sacral neuromodulation device placement
A midurethral sling
Injection of onabotulinumtoxinA into the detrusor
items.explanation: Stress incontinence from urethral hypermobility or sphincter weakness is treated surgically after conservative measures fail, and the retropubic or transobturator midurethral sling has the highest long-term success and the least morbidity. Anterior repair has lower cure rates. Neuromodulation and detrusor botulinum toxin treat refractory urgency incontinence and overactive bladder, which are not the diagnosis in this patient.

items.stem: A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman asks how much calcium she needs daily. Which recommendation is appropriate?
options: Under 500 mg total daily
About 1,200 mg total daily from diet and supplements, favoring diet
An extra 2,000 mg of supplements on top of diet
No calcium, since it raises fracture risk
items.explanation: Postmenopausal women need about 1,200 mg of calcium daily from all sources, with dietary sources preferred and supplements used only to fill the gap, because excessive supplementation raises kidney stone risk without further bone benefit. An intake under 500 mg is inadequate, and adding 2,000 mg of supplements risks exceeding the upper limit. Calcium does not raise fracture risk.

items.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 31 weeks has fever, myalgia, and diarrhea 2 days after eating unpasteurized soft cheese. Which is the best management?
options: Oral ciprofloxacin for 5 days
Supportive care with oral hydration only
Blood cultures and intravenous ampicillin
Oral doxycycline for 7 days
items.explanation: Listeria monocytogenes causes a flu-like illness in pregnancy that can lead to stillbirth, preterm birth, and neonatal sepsis, so with a compatible exposure she is evaluated with blood cultures and treated empirically with intravenous ampicillin. Supportive care alone risks fetal infection, and ciprofloxacin and doxycycline are avoided in pregnancy and lack reliable activity against the organism.

items.stem: A 31-year-old woman has a frothy green vaginal discharge, vulvar irritation, and a strawberry cervix. A wet mount shows motile flagellated organisms. Which is the best treatment?
options: Oral fluconazole 150 mg as a single dose
Clindamycin vaginal cream at bedtime for 7 days
Intramuscular ceftriaxone 500 mg once
Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
items.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis is treated in women with oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days, which is more effective than a single 2 g dose. Partners are treated at the same time and retesting is done in 3 months. Fluconazole treats candidiasis, clindamycin cream is used for bacterial vaginosis and does not reliably cure trichomoniasis, and ceftriaxone treats gonorrhea.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman scores 16 on the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 at a routine visit and describes 6 weeks of low mood, poor sleep, and loss of interest. She denies suicidal thoughts and has no history of mania. Which is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Antidepressant therapy plus psychotherapy
A daily benzodiazepine
Reassurance and rescreening at the next annual visit
Psychiatric hospital admission for observation
items.explanation: A score of 15 to 19 indicates moderately severe depression, and with no suicidal thoughts or mania the first step is an antidepressant such as a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor together with psychotherapy, because combined treatment outperforms either alone. Benzodiazepines do not treat depressive illness and carry a dependence risk, rescreening in a year ignores established disease, and admission is reserved for imminent danger to self or others.

items.stem: Immediately after placental delivery in a 30-year-old G4P3, a large vaginal mass appears, the fundus cannot be palpated, and the patient becomes hypotensive and pale. Oxytocin is running. What is the first step?
options: Increase the oxytocin rate and apply cord traction
Give carboprost and begin uterine massage
Pack the vagina and transfer for laparotomy
Stop oxytocin and replace the uterus manually
items.explanation: Acute uterine inversion causes hemorrhage and neurogenic shock. The principle is immediate manual replacement of the fundus through the cervix, ideally before a constriction ring forms, while discontinuing uterotonics that would tighten the ring. Tocolytic or general anesthesia agents may be needed to relax the uterus if replacement fails. Uterotonics, massage, or packing before replacement trap the inverted fundus, and laparotomy is a later option.

items.stem: A 25-year-old G1P0 at 9 weeks has a missed abortion confirmed by ultrasonography with a crown-rump length of 20 mm and no cardiac activity. She is stable, afebrile, and prefers to avoid surgery. Which regimen is most effective for medical management?
options: Methotrexate followed by misoprostol
Misoprostol 25 mcg orally every 6 hours
Mifepristone followed by misoprostol
Oxytocin infusion at home for 24 hours
items.explanation: The most effective medical regimen for early pregnancy loss is mifepristone 200 mg orally followed by misoprostol 800 mcg vaginally, with misoprostol alone as a reasonable alternative. Aspiration is preferred for heavy bleeding, instability, or infection. Methotrexate is used for ectopic pregnancy and gestational trophoblastic disease, a low oral misoprostol dose is too weak to expel a retained pregnancy, and oxytocin is not an expulsive regimen for the first trimester.

items.stem: A 26-year-old G2P1 at 29 weeks has regular contractions and is 5 cm dilated. Delivery is expected within hours. In addition to antenatal betamethasone, which drug lowers the risk of cerebral palsy in the neonate?
options: Nifedipine
Magnesium sulfate
Indomethacin
Terbutaline
items.explanation: Magnesium sulfate given to women at risk of delivery before 32 weeks provides fetal neuroprotection and reduces the risk of moderate to severe cerebral palsy. It is used for neuroprotection, not tocolysis, and toxicity is monitored by reflexes, respiratory rate, and urine output. Nifedipine, indomethacin, and terbutaline are tocolytics that delay delivery by roughly 48 hours but do not improve neurologic outcome, and terbutaline has maternal cardiac risks.

items.stem: A 14-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhea and short stature. She has a webbed neck and absent breast development. Follicle-stimulating hormone is elevated. Which evaluation is most important after confirming the karyotype?
options: Echocardiography or cardiac MRI to look for aortic abnormalities
Pelvic MRI to look for a pituitary adenoma
Repeat prolactin measurement in six weeks
Serial testosterone levels
items.explanation: Turner syndrome (45,X) causes gonadal dysgenesis with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, and affected girls need cardiac imaging because of bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation, and aortic root dilation, plus renal ultrasonography and thyroid, celiac, and hearing surveillance. Hyperprolactinemia and pituitary tumors cause low gonadotropins. Testosterone monitoring is not the key concern, and estrogen replacement is started to induce puberty.

items.stem: A 30-year-old G2P1 at 33 0/7 weeks reports a gush of fluid. Sterile speculum examination shows pooling, and nitrazine and ferning are positive. She has no contractions, the fetus is cephalic with a reassuring tracing, and there are no signs of infection. What is the best management?
options: Discharge home with bed rest, pelvic rest, and weekly clinic visits until she reaches 37 weeks
Start magnesium tocolysis and aim to prolong pregnancy to 37 weeks
Induce labor now without corticosteroids or antibiotics
Admit, give corticosteroids and latency antibiotics, and plan delivery at 34 0/7 weeks
items.explanation: With preterm rupture of membranes before 34 weeks and no infection, abruption, or fetal compromise, expectant management in hospital is recommended with antenatal corticosteroids, a latency antibiotic regimen, and Group B streptococcus prophylaxis as indicated. Delivery is advised at 34 0/7 weeks. Outpatient care is unsafe because of cord prolapse and infection risk, and tocolysis for a ruptured membrane offers no neonatal benefit. Immediate induction without steroids ignores a chance to improve outcomes.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome wants to conceive. She has anovulation, and her thyroid-stimulating hormone and prolactin are normal. Which agent is now preferred as first-line ovulation induction?
options: Letrozole
Clomiphene citrate
Metformin alone
Laparoscopic ovarian drilling
items.explanation: Letrozole is now the first-line agent for ovulation induction in polycystic ovary syndrome because it produces higher live birth rates with fewer multiple gestations than clomiphene citrate. Metformin may improve metabolic features but is a weaker ovulation agent. Gonadotropins and laparoscopic ovarian drilling are second-line options, used when the first-line agents fail to produce ovulation or a pregnancy.

items.stem: A 35-year-old G3P2 with asthma and normal blood pressure has persistent bleeding from uterine atony 15 minutes after delivery. Fundal massage and oxytocin have failed. Which second-line drug is most appropriate?
options: Carboprost tromethamine
Methylergonovine
A rapid bolus of high-dose oxytocin
Terbutaline
items.explanation: Methylergonovine is a strong uterotonic and is appropriate when blood pressure is normal, but it is contraindicated in hypertension and preeclampsia because of vasoconstriction. Carboprost causes bronchospasm and is avoided in asthma. Misoprostol is a reasonable alternative with fewer contraindications. A rapid oxytocin bolus risks hypotension without added benefit, and terbutaline relaxes the uterus, which would worsen atony and bleeding.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman with a high antral follicle count and an estradiol of 5,000 pg/mL is undergoing in vitro fertilization. Which strategy most effectively reduces her risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome?
options: hCG trigger and fresh embryo transfer
Doubling the gonadotropin dose
GnRH agonist trigger with freezing of all embryos
Luteal support with extra hCG injections
items.explanation: Hyperstimulation arises from vascular endothelial growth factor release driven by hCG. A GnRH agonist trigger causes a short luteinizing hormone surge and, with elective freezing of embryos, nearly eliminates severe disease. An hCG trigger carries the highest risk, and fresh transfer in a pregnancy prolongs stimulation through endogenous hCG. More gonadotropin and added hCG both worsen risk.

items.stem: A 27-year-old G1P0 has an uncomplicated twin pregnancy. Ultrasonography at 12 weeks showed a single placenta with a thin membrane between the fetuses and a T sign. Both fetuses are growing normally. When is delivery recommended?
options: 32 0/7 to 33 6/7 weeks
38 0/7 to 38 6/7 weeks
40 0/7 to 41 0/7 weeks
34 0/7 to 37 6/7 weeks
items.explanation: A single placenta with a thin membrane and a T sign is monochorionic diamniotic, whose uncomplicated twins carry a higher late stillbirth risk than dichorionic twins and are delivered at 34 0/7 to 37 6/7 weeks. Dichorionic twins are delivered at 38 0/7 to 38 6/7 weeks. Monochorionic monoamniotic twins are delivered earlier, from 32 weeks, and continuing a twin pregnancy beyond term is not recommended.

items.stem: A 53-year-old woman has postmenopausal bleeding, and endometrial biopsy shows atypical hyperplasia (endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia). She has completed childbearing, has a body mass index of 41 kg/m2, and has no medical contraindication to surgery. What is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Total hysterectomy
Oral progestin therapy for 3 months with repeat biopsy
Endometrial ablation to remove the abnormal lining
Weight loss alone with repeat biopsy in one year
items.explanation: Atypical hyperplasia, now called endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia, is a precursor of endometrial carcinoma, and a coexisting cancer is found in a substantial minority at hysterectomy. Total hysterectomy is definitive for a woman who has finished childbearing and can tolerate surgery. Progestin therapy is reserved for those who want fertility or cannot have surgery, ablation cannot treat the disease reliably, and observation risks progression.

items.stem: A 28-year-old G1P0 at 31 weeks has an estimated fetal weight below the 3rd percentile. Amniotic fluid volume is normal and umbilical artery Doppler shows absent end-diastolic flow with a reassuring nonstress test. Which plan is best?
options: Weekly testing with delivery at 38 0/7 to 39 6/7 weeks
Twice-weekly testing with delivery at 37 0/7 weeks
Corticosteroids, frequent fetal testing, and delivery at 33 0/7 to 34 0/7 weeks
Inpatient surveillance with delivery at 30 0/7 to 32 0/7 weeks
items.explanation: Absent end-diastolic flow signals placental insufficiency with severe growth restriction. The plan is antenatal corticosteroids, frequent testing or admission, and delivery between 33 0/7 and 34 0/7 weeks. Normal Doppler allows delivery at 38 to 39 weeks, an elevated systolic to diastolic ratio allows delivery at 37 weeks, and reversed end-diastolic flow moves delivery earlier, to roughly 30 to 32 weeks. Prolonging absent flow toward term raises the risk of stillbirth.

items.stem: A 37-year-old woman who smokes one pack of cigarettes daily asks for contraception. She has no other medical problems and wants a method that is highly effective and easy to maintain. Which option is most appropriate?
options: Combined oral contraceptive pill
Levonorgestrel intrauterine device
Transdermal estrogen patch
Combined vaginal ring
items.explanation: Women who are 35 or older and smoke 15 or more cigarettes daily have an unacceptable cardiovascular risk with estrogen-containing contraceptives (category 4 in the medical eligibility criteria). The pill, patch, and ring all contain estrogen. A levonorgestrel intrauterine device is a long-acting reversible method with failure rates below 1% and no estrogen, so it is safe in smokers.

items.stem: A 26-year-old G1P0 at 38 weeks reports a gush of clear fluid 2 hours ago. Pooling and ferning are confirmed. She has no contractions, the cervix is closed, the tracing is reassuring, and her group B streptococcus status is unknown. What is the best management?
options: Expectant management at home for 5 days with daily visits
Cesarean birth now because the cervix is unfavorable
Induce labor and give intravenous penicillin during labor
A 7-day course of latency antibiotics and delivery at 41 weeks
items.explanation: Once the pregnancy reaches 37 weeks, rupture of membranes without labor is managed by induction soon after presentation, because waiting raises the risk of intraamniotic infection without improving outcome. Unknown group B streptococcus status is treated as positive, so penicillin is given in labor. An unfavorable cervix is not an indication for cesarean birth, and latency antibiotics belong to preterm rupture far from term.

items.stem: A 31-year-old woman has had four episodes of vulvar itching with thick white discharge in the past year, each confirmed by wet mount and culture as Candida albicans. She is not pregnant and her glucose is normal. After a 10 to 14 day azole induction course, which maintenance plan is recommended?
options: Oral fluconazole 150 mg as one dose each month
Vaginal clindamycin cream for 7 nights
Oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
Oral fluconazole 150 mg once weekly for 6 months
items.explanation: Four or more symptomatic episodes in a year define recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis, treated with an induction course of an azole for 10 to 14 days and then suppressive fluconazole 150 mg weekly for 6 months. One dose a month is too infrequent to prevent relapse. Clindamycin and metronidazole treat bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis, not yeast, and antibacterial therapy can even promote candidal overgrowth.

items.stem: An Rh(D) negative woman with a negative antibody screen delivers an Rh(D) positive infant. A Kleihauer-Betke test shows 1.2 percent fetal red cells in her circulation. How many vials of 300 mcg anti-D immune globulin should she receive?
options: One vial
Three vials
Two vials
Six vials
items.explanation: A result of 1.2 percent suggests a fetomaternal hemorrhage of about 60 mL of fetal whole blood, calculated as the percentage times 50. One vial covers about 30 mL, so 60 mL requires 2 vials, and one extra vial is added as a margin for estimation error, giving 3. The standard single vial protects only against about 30 mL, and giving two vials leaves no margin for error in the estimate.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 6 weeks by dates has pelvic pain. She is hemodynamically stable. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows a 3 cm right tubal mass with a yolk sac and cardiac activity, and hCG is 5,200 mIU/mL. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Laparoscopic surgery
Single dose methotrexate
Expectant management with repeat hCG
Dilation and curettage
items.explanation: Fetal cardiac activity in an ectopic pregnancy is a contraindication to methotrexate, as are an ectopic mass larger than 3.5 cm and hCG above 5,000 in many protocols. Surgery, usually laparoscopic salpingectomy or salpingostomy, is indicated in this stable patient. Expectant care is reserved for low and declining hCG values, and methotrexate fails more often at this size. Curettage would not remove a tubal pregnancy.

items.stem: A 38-year-old woman at 11 weeks has cell-free DNA screening reported as high risk for trisomy 21. She is anxious and asks whether the baby definitely has Down syndrome. What is the best counseling?
options: The result is diagnostic, so no further testing is needed
It is a screening test, and diagnostic testing can confirm the result
The result should be disregarded because nuchal translucency is normal
Repeating the cell-free DNA test in two weeks will confirm the diagnosis
items.explanation: Cell-free DNA has high sensitivity for trisomy 21 but is a screening test, because placental mosaicism and maternal factors cause false positives, especially at older ages in low prevalence settings. A positive result should be followed by diagnostic testing with chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis. A normal nuchal translucency does not negate it, and repeating the same screening test does not provide a diagnosis.

items.stem: A 38-year-old woman has a routine cotest with cytology negative for intraepithelial lesion and a negative high-risk HPV result. Her prior screening results were all normal. When should her next cervical cancer screening occur?
options: In 5 years
In 1 year
In 3 years with cytology alone
At the next well-woman visit in 2 years
items.explanation: For women 30 to 65, cotesting with a negative result on both tests can be repeated every 5 years, as can primary HPV testing, while cytology alone is repeated every 3 years. Annual screening exposes patients to unnecessary colposcopy without any added benefit. The 3 year interval applies to cytology alone, and a 2 year interval is not part of current guidelines.

items.stem: A 29-year-old G3P1 woman at 26 weeks has an anti-D antibody titer of 1:32, above the critical titer of 1:16 for her laboratory. The father is heterozygous for D. What is the next best step?
options: Amniocentesis for bilirubin by optical density every week
Immediate intrauterine transfusion
Serial middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity Doppler
Plasmapheresis with delivery planned at 32 weeks
items.explanation: Once the titer exceeds the critical value, fetal anemia is assessed noninvasively with serial Doppler measurement of middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity, with values above 1.5 multiples of the median suggesting moderate to severe anemia. Amniocentesis for bilirubin has been largely replaced because of procedural risk. Transfusion is indicated only if anemia is shown. Plasmapheresis has no established role here.

items.stem: A 34-year-old woman with a germline MSH2 mutation has completed childbearing. She asks how to lower her risk of gynecologic cancer. Which recommendation is most appropriate?
options: Annual transvaginal ultrasonography and CA 125 alone
Annual Pap smears
Combined oral contraceptive use only
Hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
items.explanation: Lynch syndrome confers a lifetime endometrial cancer risk of about 40 to 60% and a significant ovarian cancer risk. Risk-reducing hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy after childbearing is recommended, commonly around age 40. Surveillance by ultrasonography and CA 125 has not been shown to be effective. Pap smears screen for cervical disease. Oral contraceptives lower risk but do not replace surgery.

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman is 5 days postpartum after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. She returns with a severe headache and blurred vision. Blood pressure is 168/112 mm Hg, repeated 20 minutes later and unchanged. She had normal pressures throughout pregnancy. What is the most important next step?
options: Reassurance and analgesics for presumed tension headache
Epidural blood patch
Magnesium sulfate and urgent blood pressure control
Discharge on oral nifedipine with a repeat blood pressure visit in one week
items.explanation: New severe hypertension with headache and visual symptoms after delivery is postpartum preeclampsia with severe features and carries a risk of eclampsia and stroke. Treatment is magnesium sulfate seizure prophylaxis plus prompt labetalol, hydralazine, or oral nifedipine. Tension headache and a blood patch are wrong diagnoses. Discharge with delayed follow up leaves severe range pressure and neurologic symptoms unaddressed.

items.stem: A 15-year-old girl has an 18 cm adnexal mass. Alpha-fetoprotein is markedly elevated, hCG is normal, and histology shows Schiller-Duval bodies. Which tumor is most likely?
options: Dysgerminoma
Immature teratoma
Granulosa cell tumor
Endodermal sinus (yolk sac) tumor
items.explanation: An ovarian germ cell tumor in an adolescent with markedly raised alpha-fetoprotein and Schiller-Duval bodies is a yolk sac tumor, which grows rapidly and responds to combination chemotherapy. Dysgerminoma typically raises lactate dehydrogenase and may mildly raise hCG. Immature teratoma shows primitive neural tissue and a normal marker profile, and granulosa cell tumor secretes inhibin and estrogen.

items.stem: A 30-year-old with diet-controlled gestational diabetes, normal fetal growth, and normal fluid reaches 39 weeks with no other complications. Which management is recommended?
options: Delivery is not advised before 39 0/7 weeks, and expectant management may continue to 40 6/7 weeks
Induction of labor at 37 weeks
Cesarean delivery at 38 weeks
Induction of labor at 34 weeks
items.explanation: For well-controlled gestational diabetes managed by diet alone, delivery should not occur before 39 0/7 weeks, and expectant management may continue through 40 6/7 weeks unless another indication arises. Induction at 37 or 34 weeks adds neonatal respiratory morbidity without benefit, and cesarean at 38 weeks has no obstetric indication here. Timing recommendations differ for insulin-treated disease, so classification of the diabetes matters here.

items.stem: Six weeks after evacuation of a complete mole, a woman has weekly hCG levels of 5,200, 5,100, 5,300, and 5,150 mIU/mL, and imaging shows no metastases. What is the diagnosis and treatment?
options: Normal regression, with continued weekly monitoring
Low-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, treated with single-agent chemotherapy
Repeat suction curettage as the only treatment
High-risk disease requiring multiagent chemotherapy
items.explanation: An hCG plateau over 3 weeks after molar evacuation defines gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. With no metastases it is low risk, and methotrexate or dactinomycin gives very high cure rates. Normal regression shows steadily falling values, so monitoring alone is wrong. Repeat curettage rarely cures a plateau, and multiagent therapy is reserved for high-risk scores. Staging by prognostic score then decides whether single-agent therapy is enough.

items.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 26 weeks has left calf swelling for two days. Compression duplex ultrasonography shows a thrombus in the femoral vein. She has no bleeding risk. What is the best treatment plan?
options: Therapeutic anticoagulation through pregnancy and 6 weeks postpartum
Warfarin throughout the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
Anticoagulation for 2 weeks followed by observation alone
Inferior vena cava filter placement alone with no medication
items.explanation: Acute deep venous thrombosis in pregnancy is treated with therapeutic anticoagulation using an agent that does not cross the placenta, continued through pregnancy and for at least 6 weeks postpartum, with a total of at least 3 months. Warfarin crosses the placenta and is teratogenic. A short course risks extension and embolism. A filter alone does not treat the thrombus and is reserved for contraindication to anticoagulation.

items.stem: A 78-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment has urgency urinary incontinence and nocturia that has not improved with timed voiding. Which pharmacologic treatment is preferred?
options: Oxybutynin
Mirabegron
Tolterodine
Imipramine
items.explanation: Anticholinergic bladder drugs are associated with cognitive decline and are avoided in older adults with impairment. The beta-3 agonist mirabegron treats overactive bladder without central anticholinergic effects, though blood pressure should be monitored. Oxybutynin crosses the blood-brain barrier and is the most harmful of the group. Tolterodine carries a similar risk, and imipramine, a tricyclic antidepressant, has anticholinergic, sedating, and cardiac effects that make it a poor choice.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 8 weeks of gestation has newly diagnosed Graves disease with palpitations, weight loss, and a suppressed TSH. Which antithyroid drug is preferred at this gestational age?
options: Methimazole
Radioactive iodine
Levothyroxine
Propylthiouracil
items.explanation: Methimazole carries a risk of embryopathy (aplasia cutis, choanal atresia) during organogenesis, so propylthiouracil is preferred in the first trimester, then many clinicians switch to methimazole to limit hepatotoxicity. Radioactive iodine is contraindicated in pregnancy because it ablates the fetal thyroid. Levothyroxine treats hypothyroidism and would worsen thyrotoxicosis in a patient with excess thyroid hormone.

items.stem: A 62-year-old sexually active woman had a hysterectomy 8 years ago and now has stage III vaginal vault prolapse with a bulge she finds bothersome. She is healthy and wants the most durable repair. Which procedure is most appropriate?
options: Anterior colporrhaphy alone to correct the bulge
Colpocleisis
Sacrocolpopexy
Kegel exercises only, with no operation planned
items.explanation: Abdominal or laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy has the lowest recurrence rate for apical prolapse and preserves vaginal length and function, with mesh erosion as a recognized risk. Anterior repair alone does not support the apex. Colpocleisis is obliterative and appropriate only for women who will not have vaginal intercourse. Pelvic floor exercises are insufficient for advanced prolapse.

items.stem: A 33-year-old G3P2 at 37 weeks reports sudden constant abdominal pain with dark vaginal bleeding, and screening confirms cocaine use. The uterus is firm and tender, the cervix is 2 cm dilated, and the tracing shows recurrent late decelerations with minimal variability. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Tocolysis with magnesium sulfate to stop the contractions
Expectant management with bed rest and serial ultrasonography
Amniotomy and oxytocin augmentation with continued observation
Emergency cesarean birth with resuscitation for hemorrhage
items.explanation: Painful dark bleeding, a firm tender uterus, and frequent contractions indicate placental abruption, and cocaine is a recognized risk factor. A category III tracing in a term fetus remote from delivery calls for emergency cesarean birth, with resuscitation for hemorrhage and coagulopathy prepared. Tocolysis can mask or worsen abruption, expectant care ignores fetal compromise, and augmenting a labor far from delivery delays rescue of the fetus.

items.stem: A 23-year-old woman has a biopsy-proven CIN 2 lesion on colposcopy. She has no prior abnormal results and wants to have children. Which management is acceptable?
options: Immediate hysterectomy to remove the lesion completely
Repeat HPV testing alone in 5 years
Observation with repeat colposcopy every 6 months
Cold knife conization now
items.explanation: In women 21 to 24 years of age, CIN 2 may be observed with colposcopy and cytology every 6 months for up to 24 months because most lesions regress and excisional treatment raises later preterm birth risk. Treatment is preferred when CIN 3 is found or when the lesion persists or progresses. Hysterectomy and conization are overtreatment. A 5 year interval is far too long for a known lesion.

items.stem: A 22-year-old woman at 20 weeks has a painless genital ulcer and a positive rapid plasma reagin with a confirmatory treponemal test. She has no known drug allergies. What is the correct treatment?
options: Azithromycin 2 g orally as a single dose at the clinic
Benzathine penicillin G, 2.4 million units once
Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 14 days
Ceftriaxone 1 g intramuscularly daily for 3 days
items.explanation: Penicillin is the only recommended therapy in pregnancy because it treats the fetus and prevents congenital syphilis. Primary syphilis requires a single 2.4 million unit dose of benzathine penicillin G. Allergic women are desensitized rather than given alternatives. Azithromycin has documented resistance and poor placental transfer. Doxycycline is avoided in pregnancy, and ceftriaxone is not a validated substitute.

items.stem: A 43-year-old woman notices green-brown, nonbloody discharge from several ducts of both nipples only when they are squeezed. Examination and mammography are normal, and prolactin is normal. What is the best management?
options: Reassurance with routine screening
Surgical excision of the central ducts
Antibiotics for 14 days
Breast MRI with biopsy of both breasts
items.explanation: Bilateral, multiduct, nonspontaneous discharge that is green, brown, or milky is usually physiologic or due to duct ectasia, and with normal examination, imaging, and prolactin it needs only reassurance and routine screening. Surgery is for spontaneous unilateral single-duct bloody discharge. Antibiotics treat nothing here, and biopsy of both breasts is invasive and unjustified. Reassurance should be paired with advice to return if the discharge becomes bloody.

items.stem: A 28-year-old G1P0 woman delivers vaginally with a laceration that involves the anal sphincter complex but not the rectal mucosa. After repair, which management is most appropriate?
options: Daily enemas to keep the bowel regular
Stool softeners and one dose of cefotetan
No antibiotics and a low-fiber diet to reduce stool
Early digital rectal examination every day for healing
items.explanation: Third-degree lacerations are repaired in layers, and a single perioperative dose of a second-generation cephalosporin lowers wound complications. Stool softeners avoid straining that stresses the repair. Enemas, rectal manipulation, and constipating diets can disrupt the repair or cause hard stools. Follow up at the postpartum visit should assess continence, and physical therapy referral may be offered.

items.stem: A 32-year-old G2P1 with one prior low transverse cesarean is in a trial of labor at 5 cm on oxytocin.
